title: Canonical signed K-flat derived tensor braiding
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category with derived category $D(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $\mathcal C$ is Grothendieck abelian in its morphism universe, monoidal [def-sfb-monoidal-category], closed, monoidal preadditive and braided, and has functorial flat resolutions. Use its existing K-flat derived tensor monoidal structure on $D(\mathcal C)$. Define $\beta^L_{K,M}:K\otimes^L M\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes^L K$ to be exactly the canonical localization braiding $\operatorname{DerivedMonoidal.braiding}'(Q_h,W)(K,M)$, where $Q_h:K(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal C)$ is the homotopy-category localization and $W$ is the class of quasi-isomorphisms. The braiding being localized is the signed total-complex braiding, given by $(-1)^{pq}\beta$ on the summand of bidegree $(p,q)$. This defines the specified isomorphism, including its inverse, by the existing derived-functor lift of that braiding; no braided structure is chosen. For symmetric coefficients this is the derived tensor symmetry used in the tensor mates and reassociations.
